posts.title: Wipe an old phone safely

slides.text:
Wipe an old phone safely
Back up what you want to keep

Back up what you want to keep — A factory reset erases the whole phone — so export photos and messages to your cloud sync, or copy everything to a cable/bluetooth transfer. Skipping this is how the new phone turns out to be missing a year of memories.

Sign out of all accounts first — Log out of Google, Apple, banking and social apps BEFORE the wipe. An account left signed in can lock the new owner out, and a signed-in session survives on the phone's login data even after some resets.

Turn off Find My Device — iOS: Settings > your name > Find My iPhone — switch it off (activation lock ties the phone to your Apple ID after a reset). Android: remove the Google account and disable Find My Device, or the next person can hit a hard FRP lock.

Factory reset — not just delete — Settings > System > Reset > Erase all data (factory reset). 'Delete' in a file manager only frees space — remnants stay. On iPhone the wipe also unsyncs your iCloud and wipes the list of trusted devices.

Verify it asks for fresh setup, then pass it on. — A clean wipe boots straight into the 'hello' / fresh-setup screen with no lock or accounts. If it ever asks for a password during setup, the reset didn't fully work — redo it before handing the phone over.
Save this — you'll need it next time.
